source_text:
Ἀδελφοὶ οὖν, ἤδη ποτὲ μετανοήσωμεν, νήψωμεν ἐπὶ τὸ ἀγαθόν: μεστοὶ γάρ ἐσμεν πολλῆς ἀνοίας καὶ πονηρίας. ἐξαλείψωμεν ἀφ̓ ἡμῶν τὰ πρότερα ἁμαρτήματα καὶ μετανοήσαντες ἐκ ψυχῆς σωθῶμεν, καὶ μὴ γινώμεθα ἀνθρωπάρεσκοι μηδὲ θέλωμεν μόνον ἑαυτοῖς ἀρέσκειν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς ἔξω ἀνθρώποις ἐπὶ τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ, ἵνα τὸ ὄνομα δἰ ἡμᾶς μὴ βλασφημῆται.
λέγει γὰρ ὁ κύριος: Διὰ παντὸς τὸ ὄνομά μου βλασφημεῖται ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, καὶ πάλιν: Οὐαὶ δἰ ὃν βλασφημεῖται τὸ ὄνομά μου. ἐν τίνι βλασφημεῖται; ἐν τῷ μὴ ποιεῖν ὑμᾶς ἃ βούλομαι.
τὰ ἔθνη γὰρ ἀκούοντα ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ἡμῶν τὰ λόγια τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς καλὰ καὶ μεγάλα θαυμάζει: ἔπειτα καταμαθόντα τὰ ἔργα ἡμῶν ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἄξια τῶν ῥημάτων ὧν λέγομεν, ἔνθεν εἰς βλασφημίαν τρέπονται, λέγοντες εἶναι μῦθόν τινα καὶ πλάνην.
ὅταν γὰρ ἀκούσωσιν παῤ ἡμῶν, ὅτι λέγει ὁ θεός: Οὐ χάρις ὑμῖν, εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, ἀλλὰ χάρις ὑμῖν, εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς καὶ τοὺς μισοῦντας ὑμᾶς: ταῦτα ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν, θαυμάζουσιν τὴν ὑπερβολὴν τῆς ἀγαθότητος: ὅταν δὲ ἴδωσιν, ὅτι οὐ μόνον τοὺς μισοῦντας οὐκ ἀγαπῶμεν, ἀλλ’ ὅτι οὐδὲ τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας, καταγελῶσιν ἡμῶν, καὶ βλασφημεῖται τὸ ὄνομα.
orientation: The preacher has just opened his homily by urging the congregation to repay Christ's saving mercy with deeds, and now turns to the danger that their bad conduct brings God's name into disrepute among outsiders.
pass_a_gloss: Brothers therefore, already at some time let us repent, let us be sober toward the good: for we are full of much folly and wickedness. Let us wipe away from us the former sins and having repented from [the] soul let us be saved, and let us not become men-pleasers nor let us wish only to please ourselves, but also the outside men in the righteousness, in order that the name through us may not be blasphemed. For the Lord says: Through all [time] my name is blasphemed among all the nations, and again: Woe through whom my name is blasphemed. In what is it blasphemed? In your not doing what I wish. For the nations hearing from our mouth the oracles of God as beautiful and great marvel; then having observed our works that they are not worthy of the words which we speak, from there they turn to blasphemy, saying [it] to be a myth and a delusion. For whenever they hear from us that God says: No grace [is] to you if you love those who love you, but grace [is] to you if you love the enemies and those who hate you: these things whenever they hear, they marvel at the excess of the goodness; but whenever they see that not only do we not love those who hate, but that not even those who love, they laugh at us, and the name is blasphemed.

choices.why: The combination conveys urgency and finality, fitting the homiletic call to stop delaying repentance.
The preposition with the accusative expresses purpose or goal, and 'good' as a substantive keeps the moral sense.
The phrase means wholeheartedly or sincerely; keeping 'soul' preserves the biblical idiom of inner sincerity.
The compound means those who seek to please human beings rather than God; the hyphenated English captures the compound structure.
The phrase 'those outside' is a standard early Christian term for non-believers; 'outsiders' is idiomatic and clear.

choices.english: There is no credit to you
choices.why: The Greek idiom means 'it is no favor/credit to you'; 'credit' conveys the sense of merit or praiseworthiness in context.
rejected: It is no thanks to you

pass_b_english: So then, brothers, let us repent at last. Let us be clear-minded for what is good, because we are full of much folly and wickedness. Let us wipe away our former sins, and let us be saved by repenting from the soul. Let us not become people-pleasers, and let us not want to please only ourselves. Let us also please outsiders in righteousness, so that the name may not be blasphemed because of us.

For the Lord says: "My name is blasphemed continually among all the nations" (Isaiah 52:5), and again: "Woe to the one through whom my name is blasphemed" (cf. Isaiah 52:5; Romans 2:24). In what way is it blasphemed? In your not doing what I want.

For when the nations hear from our mouth the oracles of God, they marvel at them as beautiful and great. Then, when they observe that our deeds are not worthy of the words we speak, they turn from this to blasphemy, saying that it is some myth and delusion.

For when they hear from us that God says: "There is no credit to you if you love those who love you, but there is credit to you if you love your enemies and those who hate you" (Luke 6:32, 35), when they hear these things, they marvel at the excess of his goodness. But when they see that we not only fail to love those who hate us, but that we do not even love those who love us, they laugh at us, and the name is blasphemed.
